title: Strategic Thread Balancer: Initiative Capacity Signals & Cross-Functional OKR Air Traffic Control
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Problem: As multiple initiatives ramp for H1, engineering and design leads report frequent conflicts when capacity signals (headcount, dedicated cycles, infra slots) are not surfaced early. Outcome: Create a lightweight cross-functional 'Air Traffic Control' for company-level OKRs that exposes initiative capacity signal, risk, and runway so PMs and exec stakeholders can rebalance commitments proactively.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A living initiative capacity dashboard that shows active commitments, burn rate, and predicted slippage for company-level OKRs
2) A cadence and decision rubric for rebalancing initiatives across teams with clear owner and escalation path
3) Integration with existing planning artifacts (roadmap sheets, Confluence PRD links) and a minimum viable automation to flag >20% overcommit within a quarter
4) Pilot completed with 3 cross-functional initiatives (Console, Runtime, Dedicated) with documented reallocation decisions and measurable outcome improvements
tasks: Draft PRD and run 30-minute kickoff with Leads (PM/Eng/Design) - owner: Aisha
Define capacity signals and sources (headcount FTE, sprint capacity, Dedicated GPU pool hours, infra maintenance windows) - owner: Liam
Prototype dashboard in Looker/Metabase with a single-sheet feed of initiative commitments - owner: Data Eng
Create rebalancing playbook and escalation runbook (owners, thresholds, communication templates) - owner: Program Mgmt
Run pilot refinement cycle and collect feedback, update acceptance criteria - owner: PMs of pilot initiatives
comments: 2025-01-10 | Aisha Gupta: Created ticket. Noting recurring issue: Q4 saw 3 mid-quarter deprioritizations due to infra outages; want earlier visibility. Attaching initial problem statement and example incident timeline (Confluence link).

2025-01-20 | Liam O'Connor: Scoped capacity signals list. Proposed minimal set: FTE allocation, Sprint points committed, Dedicated GPU hours reserved, Infra blackout windows, and cross-team shared dependences. Suggest starting with a weekly export from the roadmap sheet.
2025-01-28 | Maria Chen (Design Lead): Concern — dashboard must be consumable by execs (1 slide summary) and by leads (filterable). Will provide a Figma deck with two views by 2025-02-04.

2025-02-03 | Data Eng (Samir Patel): Built prototype query and sample dashboard. Initial feed relies on manual CSV from roadmap; discussed automating via API in Phase 2. Linking prototype: https://metabase.internal/redwood/qa/initiative-capacity

2025-02-10 | Aisha Gupta: Decision to pilot with Console-Q1, Runtime-KV-Optimization, and Dedicated-Autoscaling initiatives. Goals for pilot: reduce mid-quarter scope change by 50% and detect overcommit >20% earlier than previous quarter.
2025-02-14 | Legal/Compliance: Noted no PII involved; OK for dashboards. If we add customer-linked commitments later, will require data classification review.
decisions: Start with a lightweight dashboard fed by manual exports to prove signal value before API automation (trade-off: faster feedback loop vs. temporary manual labor).
Prioritize capacity signals that are already tracked centrally (FTE, sprint points, Dedicated GPU hours) to reduce integration work for Phase 1.
Adopt a 2-tier notification threshold: yellow at 10-20% overcommit (informal rebalancing), red at >20% (exec escalation).
Pilot scope limited to 3 initiatives to keep coordination manageable and enable quick learnings.
